UAE-account Stripe customer for credit purchases
Rationale: credits always bill on UAE, so a legacy tenant needs a second Stripe customer that must not clobber the subscription customer id
New tenants default to UAE billing account and own-Stripe OAuth model
Rationale: DEFAULT change is segment-1 only, so existing trading tenants are migrated deliberately one at a time
Close the unauthenticated read of tenant secrets
Rationale: Twilio suspension root cause - RLS off plus a table-level anon SELECT exposed plaintext Twilio/Bonzah/Tesla credentials via PostgREST
Rationale: a column-level REVOKE is a no-op while the table-level SELECT stands (Postgres authorises table-OR-column)
Anon column allow-list on tenants (explicit non-secret columns only)
Secrecy by column grant, not by row filter - tenants_public_select stays USING(true)
Known residual gap: authenticated still holds table SELECT because five select(*) call sites in portal/admin would break
Go-live stamping for operators (setup_completed_at backfill plus trigger)
Rationale: live operators mislabeled Setup Mode because setup_completed_at was only ever stamped on the trial-to-active webhook path
Went-live predicate: stripe_mode=live AND stripe_account_status=active (not the legacy managed-only stripe_onboarding_complete)
Backfill timestamp capped to >2 days ago so the 24h You're Live banner does not fire retroactively
Per-category idempotency guard when generating a rental's first charges

Rationale: the portal's pre-inserted Bonzah Insurance charge tripped the coarse whole-function guard, so Rental/Tax were never created and payment bound only to Insurance (Paramount R-3bb30d, $131.33 paid, $50.13 allocated)
Invoice-to-ledger category split (Rental, Tax, Service Fee, Insurance, Delivery Fee, Collection Fee, Extras)
Accept the complete Stripe subscription status set including incomplete_expired
Rationale: one rejected status makes the handler throw, Stripe retries ~3 days then auto-disables the endpoint, killing delivery of every other subscription event
Rationale: Stripe API 2025-03-31 (basil) moved current_period_start/end onto subscription items, so unguarded reads produced new Date(NaN) RangeErrors and HTTP 500 on every subscription.updated
Sync-provenance metadata (last_stripe_event_at, last_synced_at, last_sync_source)
Out-of-order protection: an older Stripe event must never overwrite newer state, and the reconciler must not clobber fresher webhook data
Dunning fields for the grace clock (next_payment_attempt, attempt_count, billing_reason)
Rationale: due_date is NULL on all 51 invoice rows (everything is charge_automatically), so the grace clock derives from current_period_end / next_payment_attempt
Hourly pg_cron schedule for the subscription reconciler
Rationale: webhooks are a delivery guarantee, not a consistency guarantee - a 7-day handler crash left 9 tenants marked canceled who were active and one trialing who was past_due
Cadence trade-off: hourly at minute 17 bounds drift while staying inside Stripe rate limits across all four account x mode cells
Secret hygiene: the job command is cloned from an existing cron job so the service_role key is never written into a migration in source control
Per-tenant Google tag (GA4) for the booking site
Rationale: any new tenants column is unreadable to anon until added to the allow-list, so the tag would silently never load without an explicit column GRANT
Portal feedback channel (staff report bugs about the Drive247 software to super admins)
Naming boundary: tenant_feedback_* is not rental_reviews (staff rating customers) nor feedback_submissions (renter testimonials)

Attribution snapshot: app_user_id is nullable ON DELETE SET NULL, with submitter name/email/role denormalised so a departing staff member neither deletes their bug reports nor blocks their own account deletion
notified_at stamp makes the feedback alert mailer idempotent against retries and double-clicks
Own-rows-only read policy: a viewer has no business reading the head admin's complaint, so SELECT is submitter-or-super-admin rather than tenant-wide
Absent INSERT policy on insights is the control that stops a browser forging an AI summary (service-role writer only)
feedback-screenshots is a PRIVATE bucket because a portal screenshot routinely contains customer PII (names, addresses, licence images, card last4)
Structurally enforced singleton settings row (unique CHECKed boolean instead of app-level convention)
Case-insensitive recipient uniqueness so Ops@ and ops@ cannot double-mail the same person
feedback_last_prompted_at drives both prompt throttles (rental-completion cooldown and force-show-on-next-login)
Narrow screenshot reads to the submitter's own rows, matching the row policy

Rationale: the tenant-wide storage grant let any staff member list and sign every screenshot in the tenant folder, defeating the own-rows row policy; the preview it was justified by uses an in-memory object URL and never needed a storage read
source column records which entry point produced a submission (sidebar / rental_close / forced)
Rationale: source was previously smuggled into page_path, corrupting the only reproduction field so any filter or GROUP BY silently missed prompted submissions
SECURITY DEFINER stamp so the portal never needs a direct UPDATE grant on app_users

Rationale: the self-UPDATE policy authorising the browser write carries no column list, so it also lets any portal user set their own is_super_admin - routing the stamp through a function lets that policy be narrowed
Platform Terms of Service acceptance recorded against the operator (tenant)

Rationale: terms_version / policies_accepted_at / policy_acceptances are a different system (the tenant's own policy accepted by their staff) and the settings page NULLs policies_accepted_at on every version edit, so reuse would wipe the evidence and corrupt the staff login gate

Deliberately no anon grant: these columns must never enter TENANT_CORE_COLUMNS, because Postgres refuses the whole row when one selected column is ungranted and that already took down login and branding once (customer_theme_mode)
Accepted ToS version is derived server-side and never taken from the request body; accepted_by is intentionally not a FK so the audit record survives user deletion
Stamp tenant_id on every vehicle-lifecycle P&L writer and backfill the orphans
Rationale: a tenant_id-NULL P&L row falls outside the operator's RLS scope, so the portal's cleanup delete matches nothing and the vehicle delete then fails on the FK
payment_apply_fifo_v2 already stamped tenant_id on payment-driven P&L rows; this extends the same guard to acquisition, disposal, service, plate and fine entries
Vehicle deletion unblocked: children cascade in the database, beneath RLS, atomically with the vehicle

Rationale: the portal's four unchecked non-transactional child deletes destroyed some children then failed on the FK, and re-adding the vehicle then collided with vehicles_reg_key because the original row was never removed
Decision: owner_payout_lines stays ON DELETE RESTRICT - erasing payout history to make a delete convenient is the wrong trade; operators are pointed at Dispose instead
